label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional difficulties. With 165 respondents in this cluster, the profile points to a meaningful subgroup where extensive screen time coincides with pronounced psychological distress across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores indicating frequent feelings of social disconnection
Higher depressive symptom severity suggesting persistent low mood and functional impact
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most elevated of the three distress indicators
Extended daily screen time exceeding 5 hours, potentially reflecting both cause and coping mechanism
Co-occurrence of all three distress dimensions, indicating compounded emotional burden
tone: Concerned and empathetic, acknowledging significant emotional distress across multiple domains

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below the scale midpoint, minimal PHQ-9 depression scores, and near-floor GAD-7 anxiety scores, these individuals demonstrate consistently positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or online activity
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale (mean ≈ 0.77)
Exhibits minimal depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9 (mean ≈ 0.33)
Shows near-absent anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7 (mean ≈ 0.09)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen time (1–3 hours)
Demonstrates a consistently low-distress pattern across all psychological measures

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level education or above, with moderate daily screen/internet use of 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating frequent feelings of social disconnection
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting minimal mood impairment
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating limited worry or nervousness
Moderate internet/screen engagement (1–3 hours daily), neither highly disengaged nor excessively online
Apparent decoupling between perceived social isolation and internalizing symptoms
tone: Quietly detached yet psychologically stable; socially understimulated rather than emotionally distressed
